4.OA.A.1: Interpret multiplication equations as comparisons (35 is 5 times as many as 7).
4.OA.A.2: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison.
4.OA.A.3: Solve multistep word problems with the four operations, interpret remainders, write equations with a letter, and check reasonableness.
4.OA.A.3.a: Know multiplication facts and related division facts through 12 × 12.
4.OA.B.4: Find factor pairs and multiples; decide whether a whole number is prime or composite.
4.OA.C.5: Generate a number or shape pattern from a rule and identify features of the pattern.
4.NBT.A.1: Recognize that a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.
4.NBT.A.2: Read, write and compare multi-digit whole numbers using numerals, number names and expanded form.
4.NBT.A.3: Use place value to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.
4.NBT.B.4: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.
4.NBT.B.5: Multiply up to four digits by one digit, and two two-digit numbers, using place value strategies and area models.
4.NBT.B.6: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors.
4.NF.A.1: Explain why fractions are equivalent and generate equivalent fractions.
4.NF.A.2: Compare two fractions with different numerators and denominators using common denominators, common numerators or benchmarks.
4.NF.B.3.a: Understand adding and subtracting fractions as joining and separating parts of the same whole.
4.NF.B.3.b: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way.
4.NF.B.3.c: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators.
4.NF.B.3.d: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions with like denominators.
4.NF.B.4.a: Understand a fraction a/b as a multiple of 1/b.
4.NF.B.4.b: Multiply a fraction by a whole number.
4.NF.B.4.c: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number.
4.NF.C.5: Write tenths as hundredths and add fractions with denominators 10 and 100.
4.NF.C.6: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100.
4.NF.C.7: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size.
4.MD.A.1: Know relative sizes of measurement units and express larger units in terms of smaller units.
4.MD.A.2: Solve word problems involving distances, time, liquid volumes, masses and money.
4.MD.A.3: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles.
4.MD.B.4: Make a line plot of measurements in fractions of a unit and solve problems using it.
4.MD.C.5.a: Understand that an angle is measured as a fraction of a circle; a one-degree angle is 1/360 of a circle.
4.MD.C.5.b: An angle that turns through n one-degree angles has a measure of n degrees.
4.MD.C.6: Measure angles in whole-number degrees with a protractor and sketch angles of a given measure.
4.MD.C.7: Recognize angle measure as additive and find unknown angles.
4.G.A.1: Draw and identify points, lines, segments, rays, angles, and perpendicular and parallel lines.
4.G.A.2: Classify two-dimensional figures by parallel or perpendicular lines and by angle size; recognize right triangles.
4.G.A.3: Recognize and draw lines of symmetry in two-dimensional figures.
